Hi Sana / Jake — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single place for answers and action items. Let me know if I missed anything.

What we covered (high level)
- Compliance posture: Redwood has SOC 2 in flight (Type I completed; Type II planned for Q3 2026). We can provide the Type I report today under NDA and a roadmap for Type II.
- Regulatory: Redwood supports GDPR and HIPAA workloads. For HIPAA we offer a BAA for Dedicated and Private deployments; Hosted customers can be supported on a case-by-case basis (we discussed controls and scoping).
- Audit / forensic trails: key capabilities we discussed:
  - Admin activity logs (console actions, role changes, user provisioning).
  - API-level request/response logging (headers, truncated request/response bodies configurable per customer).
  - System / infra events (model routing, instance lifecycle events).
  - Export options: direct S3 export (with Object Lock option), syslog/CEF, and streamed delivery to your SIEM (Splunk/QRadar) via our connector.
  - Format & fidelity: exports are NDJSON with RFC3339 timestamps by default; we can include trace IDs and request IDs to correlate events.
  - Immutability: we support append-only export with S3 Object Lock (WORM) at customer opt-in. For hosted customers we can provide time-windowed immutable exports to a customer-owned bucket.
  - Retention: default 90 days for interactive logs; archival retention up to multi-year (configurable per contract).
  - Redaction/pseudonymization: configurable pipeline to strip or hash PII before export to satisfy GDPR/HIPAA requirements.

Attachments: Redwood_Security_Summary_2026Q1.pdf (high-level controls) and sample-log-export.ndjson (sample schema & small example).

Open questions we noted from your team
1) GDPR erasure vs immutable logs: how do we reconcile erasure requests with immutable forensic trails?
2) Key management: BYOK / KMS integration and key rotation cadence.
3) Live streaming into Splunk — latency expectations and retries.
4) Where will you accept the vendor security questionnaire (xlsx attached to your reply)?

Proposed next steps
- Connor: share SOC 2 Type I and the security summary (attached) — ACTION: done (attached).
- Grace: prepare a 15–20 minute technical deep-dive showing a sample log export and the Object Lock export flow.
- Schedule: propose Tue 6 Apr 2026 at 10:00 PT for the technical deep-dive with your security and eng reps. Please confirm availability.
- Please attach your vendor security questionnaire to this thread if you want us to complete it prior to the call.

Thanks — will update this thread with the SOC doc and any follow-up behavioral notes.

Best,
Connor

Connor / Grace — internal draft reply to Sana's questions and proposed prep for the deep-dive. I'm keeping this internal until we finalize language to send to Vantage.

Short answers / proposals:
- GDPR erasure vs immutability: offer two supported patterns:
  1) Customer-controlled export: keep the canonical, identifiable logs in a customer-owned S3 bucket with Object Lock enabled. If a subject erasure request arrives, customer can remove PII from their own mapping store; Redwood can provide pseudonymized exports where we hash or redact identity fields at export time.
  2) Split-store approach: keep minimal event metadata in Redwood (timestamps, event types, trace ids) and push enriched, identifiable logs to the customer-controlled export. This lets Redwood comply with erasure by removing the minimal identifiers while the customer retains the full forensic export under their retention policy.
- KMS/BYOK: we support cross-account AWS KMS with grants and CloudHSM-backed keys for Dedicated / Private. Hosted customers can use our managed KMS or BYOK (customer keys stored in their account). Rotation: we recommend monthly automatic rekey for session keys; CMK rotations are supported per your rotation policy, and we publish our rotation records in the key audit log.
- Splunk connector: supports HEC over TLS with exponential backoff/queueing and a configurable retry window. Typical end-to-end tail latency in our tests is ~10–20s for streaming delivery (depends on throughput).

Attachments for Vantage: Redwood_Sec_Controls_Summary.pdf (3-pager) — include this as the short control summary. Grace — can you prepare the sample export and a short demo flow showing Object Lock -> export -> sample NDJSON (include RFC3339 timestamps and trace id correlation)?

Action items (internal)
- Connor: send SOC 2 Type I and the Sec Summary to Sana (and place NDA link if needed).
- Grace: prepare demo artifacts (sample-log-export.ndjson + export runbook).
- Connor: coordinate call scheduling and invite Jake and their engineering lead. Proposed time: Tue Apr 6, 10:00 PT.

I'll draft an external reply once Grace confirms demo artifacts.
